event: Cabinet in-principle approval to lease six AAI airports via PPPAC; EGoS constituted
entity: Airports Authority of India / Union Cabinet
source_title: Cabinet approves leasing out six airports - Ahmedabad, Jaipur, Lucknow, Guwahati, Thiruvananthapuram and Mangaluru through PPP
publisher: PMIndia (PMO), copy of Cabinet decision
note: Decision-maker: Union Cabinet. In-principle approval to lease six airports for operation, management and development under PPP 'through PPPAC'; constitutes an Empowered Group of Secretaries headed by CEO NITI Aayog with Secretaries of Civil Aviation, DEA and Expenditure 'to decide on any issue falling beyond the scope of PPPAC'. Kerala HC (para 3) dates the Cabinet approval 8.11.2018; Exhibit R6(a) there is the PIB press note of 08.11.2018. PIB original not retrieved.

event: EGoS decides bid terms: no cap on airports per bidder; no prior airport experience; single-stage bidding
entity: Empowered Group of Secretaries (chair CEO NITI Aayog)
source_title: 86 Registration Were Received In the Portal for 6 Airports Under the PPP Bidding Process (Press Note, Ministry of Civil Aviation)
publisher: Press Information Bureau
note: Ministry says terms were 'deliberated and decided by the EGoS in its meeting held on 17.11.2018' and 'agreed by the PPPAC in its meeting held on 11.12.2018'; EGoS 'took a conscious decision not to put any restrictions on the number of airports to be bid for or to be awarded to a single entity' (six airports = 9.5% of traffic) and 'not to stipulate prior airport experience as a mandatory qualification to increase competition'. The EGoS minutes themselves were not found.

event: EGoS directs single-stage bidding to finish transaction by 28.02.2019 (as argued from PPPAC record)
source_title: Mahesh G. v. Union of India and connected cases, W.P.(C) 2224/2019 & 7 others, judgment of 19.10.2020 (K. Vinod Chandran and C.S. Dias JJ.)
publisher: High Court of Kerala (via Indian Kanoon)
note: Counsel for Calicut employees' union, reading para 10 of Exhibit P12 (record of 85th PPPAC meeting), submitted that 'the EGoS on 17.11.2018 directed a single stage bidding so as to complete the transaction by 28.02.2019; prior to the Code of Conduct being implemented'. This is a party's reading of the record, reported by the court; the court did not reject the fact, it held the process lawful.

event: DEA appraisal note and NITI Aayog office memorandum on the RFP, both dated 10.12.2018, forwarded to PPPAC
entity: Department of Economic Affairs; NITI Aayog
source_title: Mahesh G. v. Union of India and connected cases, W.P.(C) 2224/2019 & 7 others, judgment of 19.10.2020 (K. Vinod Chandran and C.S. Dias JJ.)
publisher: High Court of Kerala (via Indian Kanoon)
locator: paras 13, 51-54; list of exhibits in W.P.(C) 5482/2019 (P11, P13)
note: Primary documents are court exhibits, not themselves retrieved. Exhibit list: P11 'Appraisal note dated 10.12.2018, forwarded by the Department of Economic Affairs'; P13 'Office Memorandum dated 10.12.2018, forwarded by the NITI Aayog to DEA' (para 13 of the judgment labels them the other way round). Court's summary of content (para 51): one note sought review of 'the per passenger fee evaluation parameter and the technical and financial capacities'; the other raised that the two-stage procedure in the PPP Guidelines was not followed, that there was no approved Model Concession Agreement, no project cost estimate, and that the RFP was 'poorly prepared'. Court (para 52): these are 'only in the nature of recommendations' that 'can always be overruled by the PPPAC or the EGoS'; (para 54) they 'were considered by the PPPAC and the EGoS'.

event: Government denies DEA/NITI objections were overruled; says both sat on EGoS and PPPAC
source_title: 86 Registration Were Received In the Portal for 6 Airports Under the PPP Bidding Process
publisher: Press Information Bureau
note: Rebuttal of a 15.01.2021 news article. States the claim that Finance Ministry and NITI Aayog 'had recorded objection' is 'factually incorrect' because both are members of EGoS and PPPAC, and their views 'cannot be considered as overruled'. The release does not deny that the notes existed or state their content.

event: PPPAC 85th meeting approves transaction (RFP) documents
source_title: Mahesh G. v. Union of India and connected cases, W.P.(C) 2224/2019 & 7 others, judgment of 19.10.2020 (K. Vinod Chandran and C.S. Dias JJ.)
publisher: High Court of Kerala (via Indian Kanoon)
note: Record of discussion of 85th PPPAC meeting (Exhibit P12). Court notes Phase-I capex for Thiruvananthapuram under Rs 1,000 crore so the competent authority was the Minister, not CCEA (para 53); PPPAC accepted experience in any infrastructure sub-sector of DEA's Harmonised Master List, with a single project of at least Rs 1,400 crore (para 43). Petitioners alleged only two Secretaries attended (para 13); not decided by the court.

event: AAI issues RFP for six airports; bid parameter = per passenger fee; financial capacity threshold
source_title: Cabinet approves proposal for leasing out three airports - Jaipur, Guwahati and Thiruvananthapuram - of AAI through PPP
publisher: PMIndia (PMO), copy of Cabinet decision
note: Release: RFP 'released ... on 14.12.2018 through global competitive bidding wherein per passenger fee is the bidding parameter'; technical bids opened 16.02.2019, financial bids 25/26.02.2019. Rs 3,500 crore financial-capacity floor is from Kerala HC paras 13, 42. Kerala HC para 15: bid ranked on the domestic per-passenger fee, with the concessionaire paying twice that for international passengers. Right of first refusal within 10% of highest bid for a Kerala-nominated entity added by corrigendum of 28.12.2018 (Kerala HC paras 8, 30).

event: Bid participation: registrations, bidders, bids

publisher: Press Information Bureau
note: Ministry: 25 firms registered, 86 registrations, '32 bids were received from 10 difference entities for 6 airports'; Adani Enterprises' per-passenger quote 'was highest in all the six airports'. Kerala HC para 41 states '10 bidders qualified who together submitted 36 bids' — the two official figures differ (32 vs 36).

event: Kerala HC dismisses State of Kerala, KSIDC and union petitions against Thiruvananthapuram lease
source_title: Mahesh G. v. Union of India and connected cases, W.P.(C) 2224/2019 & 7 others, judgment of 19.10.2020 (K. Vinod Chandran and C.S. Dias JJ.)
publisher: High Court of Kerala (via Indian Kanoon)
note: 'there is absolutely no valid ground to cause interference'; the State and KSIDC case 'is a classic example of the proverbial sour grapes'. Holds: no promissory estoppel/legitimate expectation (paras 30-32); Rs 3,500 crore threshold and absence of airport-experience requirement not tailor-made (paras 41-43); DEA/NITI notes non-statutory recommendations (para 52). The court's 18.12.2019 order (Indian Kanoon doc 97445694) had earlier dismissed the petitions on Article 131 grounds; the Supreme Court remanded (Feb 2020, reported by LiveLaw; order not retrieved).

event: Supreme Court dismisses Kerala's SLP against HC judgment; land-ownership question left open

note: REPORTED ONLY. Bench reported as CJI U.U. Lalit and Bela M. Trivedi J.; quoted: 'Considering the fact that the private entity has been in operation since October 2021, we see no reason to interfere.' Supreme Court order not retrieved.

event: Navi Mumbai airport: CIDCO concession awarded to MIAL (lone surviving bid of two)
source_title: Report No. 4 of 2018, Public Sector Undertakings, Government of Maharashtra, Chapter III
publisher: Comptroller and Auditor General of India
note: RFQ February 2014; RFP to qualified bidders May 2016; bids opened February 2017; 'Out of the two bids received, the bid of ... MIAL ... quoted the highest gross annual revenue share of 12.60 per cent'; LoA October 2017; concession agreement January 2018 with SPV Navi Mumbai International Airport Pvt Ltd, CIDCO 26% equity capped at Rs 430 crore, concessionaire 74%. Audit finding: executing the concession 'without completing the land acquisition and pre-development works lacks justification'. Phase-I cost rose from Rs 4,424 crore (2008) to Rs 8,801 crore (2016). This predates Adani; Adani acquired NMIAL via MIAL in 2021.

event: APSEZ agrees to acquire 75% of Krishnapatnam Port Company from CVR Group

note: Negotiated private acquisition. EV Rs 13,572 crore = 10.2x FY19 EBITDA of Rs 1,330 crore; debt Rs 6,212 crore; CCI approval required; close within 120 days. Pre-deal: CVR Group 90.6%, 3i's Strategic Port Investment KPC 9.4%. CCI approval (reported July 2020) and completion date not confirmed from a primary document.

Arithmetic note: the private stakes were bought at Rs 120/share (reported); 31.5% = ~16.3 crore shares implies ~51.7 crore shares in all, so 10.4% at Rs 644.78 crore is also ~Rs 120/share. This is a computation from reported figures, not a documented valuation.

entity: Government of Kerala / Vizhinjam International Seaport Ltd

event: Vizhinjam: CAG audit findings on concession terms
entity: Comptroller and Auditor General of India
unit: INR crore (extra revenue to concessionaire from 40- vs 30-year term)
source_title: Report No. 4 of 2017, Public Sector Undertakings, Government of Kerala, Chapter III
publisher: Comptroller and Auditor General of India
note: Tabled 23.05.2017 (per CAG report page). Findings: project structure changed after pre-qualifying five bidders; 40-year term vs standard 30 gives Rs 29,217 crore extra revenue; extendable period raised from 10 to 20 years by DEA on Kerala's request (24.11.2014) — retaining 10 years would have yielded Rs 61,095 crore (PV Rs 353 crore) to the State; revenue share deferred to 15th year after COD, forgoing Rs 2,153 crore; termination payment Rs 19,555 crore would make GoK net receipts (-)Rs 5,608 crore. GoK replies (Aug 2016) recorded and rejected by audit. A judicial commission (Justice C.N. Ramachandran Nair) later found no corruption (reported Dec 2018; report not retrieved).

event: Mundra: Gujarat HC directs Centre to decide MPSEZ environmental clearance within 30 days; halts further activity meanwhile

note: PIL by Navinal villagers. 'Till such appropriate decision is taken by the Central Government, there shall not be any further activity in the form of construction etc. including the functioning of the units in the area in question'; Centre may consider the Sunita Narain Committee report. Records MoEF office memorandum of 14.09.2012 appointing the committee on complaints by Kheti Vikas Sewa Trust. Subsequent appeal history not retrieved.

event: Mundra: Sunita Narain Committee report; MoEF show-cause (30.09.2013); MoEF order (18.09.2015)
source_title: Jusab Kasam Manjaliya v. Union of India, R/Special Civil Application No. 5509 of 2019, CAV judgment of 06.02.2023
publisher: High Court of Gujarat (via Indian Kanoon)

The committee report itself (MoEF URL adani-report-290413.pdf) could not be retrieved, so its findings (75 ha mangrove loss at Bocha; restoration fund of Rs 200 crore or 1% of project cost) remain REPORTED ONLY (Down To Earth / CSE).
